audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with the packet and the already-audited mirror.
audit.why: Mirror set the sides to Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Sylas, Skill, Sylas; my layers read Skill first and gave Jayce the last two rows, so the two pages answered 'who wins level 1' and 'who wins late' differently.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 4, 5 and 6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group with ratings and the affected whys rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page claimed Hijack 'removes his ability to swap stances temporarily'.
audit.why: Riot's Hijack text is 'steals the enemy's ultimate ability and can cast it freely' — nothing says the enemy loses theirs, and Jayce's swap is a 6-second cooldown, so denial was never possible. The level-6 spike is about your burst, not about disabling him.
audit.corrected: Restated in whys[4] and mid, with the 6-second swap named so the reader knows why denial is not the plan.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid told you to 'Land Abduct, stun him', and early gave Thundering Blow a cooldown of 'roughly 13 seconds early'.
audit.why: Abduct's recast pulls Sylas to the target and applies no CC — the mirror already corrected this on their side. Thundering Blow is 20/18/16/14/12/10, so 20 seconds at rank 1, not 13; a player timing a 13-second window walks into a live knockback.
audit.corrected: Stun claim removed from mid; 20s written into early, dontsFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'take the fifteen-second invitation' — invented number; and the stance-swap armour shred was never mentioned.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1. The flagged missing interaction is his R: the first attack after swapping to Mercury Cannon reduces your armour and magic resist — that swap animation is the burst tell.
audit.corrected: 16s written in; the shred added to breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.before: At level 1 you have Q or W and zero gap-close — Jayce immediately goes Mercury Cannon stance and starts chunking you with Acceleration Gate into Q poke. Do not walk up; farm with Q Chain Lash from max range and accept the poke. Level 2 gives you E, but Jayce's E Thundering Blow knocks you back the moment you land your hook, instantly wasting your only gap-closer and resetting him to range. The core early lesson: never fire Abduct into Jayce when his E is up — watch for it to go on cooldown (short, roughly 13 seconds early), THEN hook. You are being outranged, poked, and kited; stay healthy enough to all-in at 6.
edits.after: At level 1 you have Q or W and zero gap-close — Jayce opens in Mercury Cannon and chunks you with Acceleration Gate into Shock Blast. Do not walk up; farm with Q Chain Lash from max range and accept the poke. Level 2 gives you E, but Thundering Blow knocks you back the moment you arrive, wasting your only gap-closer and resetting him to range. The core early lesson: never fire Abduct while his E is available — it is 20 seconds at rank 1, so watch it go and hook after. You are being outranged, poked and kited; stay healthy enough to all-in at 6.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are genuinely contested because your full kit W heal and Passive chain-autos can match Jayce if you survive the poke, but he still owns the approach — every time you E hook he has the threat of hammer-E knockback or a point-and-click Q through a gate to burst you. At level 6 this matchup flips for one brief window: Hijack steals Jayce's Transformation, removing his ability to swap stances temporarily and giving you a massive-damage R burst. Land Abduct, stun him, W for the missing-health execute, and proc Passive chains — Jayce with no R and no stance swap in melee range dies to this combo. Force the all-in now; you will not get a safer window.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are genuinely contested because your W heal and Petricite Burst autos can match Jayce if you survive the poke, but he still owns the approach — every time you close he has hammer-E knockback or a gated Shock Blast to burst you. At level 6 the matchup opens for one window: Hijack copies his Transformation and gives you the swap burst yourself. His own swap is a 6-second cooldown, so this is never about denying him anything — it is about your damage. Abduct pulls you onto him, W lands the missing-health hit, and passive chains finish it; Jayce caught in hammer range loses that exchange. Force the all-in now, because you will not get a safer window.
